ns2:section.sectionText: Wilderness in American Culture Explores the wilderness as a concept and a material reality in American culture and history. Examines film, literature, law and policy to understand how the concept of wilderness has figured into how Americans have made sense of their place in nature. A critical examination of both wild lands themselves, and the meanings Americans have attached to them, over time. For Chancellor's Scholars; others may enroll with consent of instructor and Director of the Campus Honors Program.
